speaker: Sandy
text: Let me be direct. Pay the full one point four by the fifteenth or I file for bankruptcy and you get nothing.

speaker: Pat
text: If you file, I call the loan the same day. Two hundred thousand, due immediately.

speaker: Riley
text: Call it. The trustee will tell you to get in line with every other creditor.

speaker: Jordan
text: And the trustee will sell your house to pay us.

text: You'd put a family on the street over a wood upgrade. Good to know who we're dealing with.

text: Nobody said that.

text: You didn't have to. Here's another one: every crew in this county hears how Pat treats contractors.

speaker: Pat
text: And every lender hears how Sandy's company walks away from loans.

speaker: Riley
text: We haven't walked away from anything. You're the one who stopped paying.

speaker: Jordan
text: We stopped paying four hundred thousand that was never approved. The rest is sitting in escrow.

speaker: Morgan
text: Escrow doesn't pay the supplier.

speaker: Sandy
text: If I don't pay the supplier, I'm done. And if I'm done, you're done, because nobody else will finish your condos.

speaker: Pat
text: That's a threat.

speaker: Sandy
text: It's arithmetic.

speaker: Sam
text: Can I say something? If this keeps going, both of you lose, and the only winner is the trustee.

speaker: Jordan
text: Here is where we are. If you do not withdraw the four hundred thousand, then we will let the court sort it out, and that takes two years you don't have.

speaker: Riley
text: And if you do not release the escrow this week, then we file, and you don't see the two hundred back.

speaker: Morgan
text: So we both have a gun on the table. Great.

speaker: Sam
text: Then let's both put them down for five minutes. Sandy, what do you actually need by the fifteenth?

speaker: Sandy
text: Ninety percent of the supplier bill. Call it a million two.

speaker: Pat
text: The escrow is one million. That's close.

speaker: Riley
text: Close doesn't keep the supplier shipping.

speaker: Sam
text: What if we release the million now and cover the other two hundred against the loan?

speaker: Sandy
text: Meaning you forgive the loan?

speaker: Pat
text: Meaning we net it. The supplier gets one point two, the loan is settled, and the four hundred is what we're still arguing about.

speaker: Morgan
text: And you'd put that in writing today.

speaker: Jordan
text: Today.

speaker: Sandy
text: Then the four hundred goes to mediation, not court.

speaker: Pat
text: Agreed. Mediation, thirty days.
